issue: GEM models the Romgaz-SOCAR Black Sea LNG project as a single terminal under Georgia (location Kulevi; UnitName 'Export Facility'; FacilityType=export). The existing ResearcherNotesUnit (RR 7/24) already anticipates a split: 'Regas project appears to be sited at Constanta, Romania ... this project should likely be split into two separate facilities.' From a Romania-coverage standpoint, the Romania-side regasification (import) facility at the Port of Constanta is not yet represented as a Romania row. Discovery sweep confirms this is the only live Romania LNG terminal lead and that it is already tracked (pending split), NOT an undiscovered gap. As of the most recent reporting (feasibility study completed and reported positive Apr 2024; project-company structure said to be pending), no FID and no firm Romania-side facility design (FSRU vs onshore) have been confirmed, so it does not yet warrant a standalone Romania import row on its own merits. Distinct from the cancelled Constanta/AGRI LNG Terminal (T100000130502).
suggested_action: Hold for the split flagged in the existing researcher note. When sponsor/financing firm up and the Constanta regasification facility's design and location are confirmed, route to an Update batch to (a) split the Georgia 'Export Facility' record from a new Romania import/regasification facility at Constanta and (b) re-verify status. Recheck ~6-12 months. Independent (non-GEM-derived) sources confirming the project and the Constanta regas siting: https://jamestown.org/romania-and-azerbaijan-mull-new-lng-project-on-the-black-sea/ (Romania-Azerbaijan LNG, Nov 2022, distinct from AGRI); https://roec.biz/project/black-sea-lng-dreams-vs-reality/ (Constanta LNG overview); https://lngprime.com/asia/romgaz-socar-plan-black-sea-lng-project/64354/ (Romgaz-Socar Black Sea LNG project, already the GEM source).
